chunks: Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from ʿAmmār ibn Marwān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Whoever travels shortens the salat (prayer) and breaks the fast, unless he is a man whose travel is for hunting, or in disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or as a messenger for one who disobeys Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or in pursuit of an enemy, or out of enmity, or for talebearing, or to cause harm to a group of the Muslims.

key_terms.سِعَايَةٍ: talebearing or carrying words to cause harm

ai.seo_question: When must a traveler shorten salat (prayer) and break the fast, and what are the exceptions?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the traveler’s duty to shorten salat (prayer) and break the fast during travel. It also lists exceptions where the journey is tied to sinful or harmful purposes, indicating that such travel does not receive the same ruling.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1979 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

Whoever travels must shorten their prayers and break their fast, except in the case of a person whose travel is for hunting, committing a sin against Allah (swt) the Almighty, acting as a messenger for someone disobedient to Allah (swt), pursuing an enemy, fostering enmity, engaging in slander, or causing harm to a group of Muslims."
